name: Markifact
description:
Markifact is a marketing automation and advertising management connector for Claude. Built for marketers, agencies, media buyers, PPC specialists, growth teams, and in-house marketing teams who need cross-channel reporting, paid media analysis, and campaign management without switching between ad dashboards.

Ad platforms: Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram), Microsoft Ads, TikTok Ads, LinkedIn Ads, Reddit Ads, Snapchat Ads, Pinterest Ads, Amazon Ads, Apple Search Ads, OpenAI Ads (ChatGPT ads), and Display & Video 360 (DV360), Spotify Ads, Data Manager.

Analytics and data: Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Google Search Console, Google Tag Manager (GTM), Google Trends, Google Search, BigQuery, SEMrush, Adjust, Bing Webmaster Tools, PageSpeed Insights

E-commerce and CRM: Shopify, HubSpot, Klaviyo, and Google Merchant Center.

Workspace and reporting: Google Sheets, Google Slides, Google Docs, Google Drive, Microsoft SharePoint (OneDrive), Dropbox, Google Business Profile, and Google Maps.

Social and messaging: Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, Slack, Pinterest, YouTube, TikTok, WhatsApp.

Use Markifact for cross-channel advertising reports, PPC reporting, campaign audits, account monitoring, budget pacing, search term and keyword analysis, creative performance analysis, marketing data extraction, and campaign optimization. Claude can retrieve campaigns, ad groups, ads, keywords, audiences, budgets, conversions, performance metrics, dimensions, and account structures from any connected account.

Markifact also supports advertising automation. Create campaigns and ads, update budgets and bids, pause or enable campaigns, edit supported ad fields, upload images and video, manage targeting, and run other platform-supported actions, then send results straight to Google Sheets, Slides, Docs, or Slack.

protocolMetadata.instructions:
Markifact provides 1000+ marketing operations across platforms like Google Ads, Meta Ads, GA4, Sheets, HubSpot, and more.
Workflow: 1) find_operations → discover exact Markifact operation IDs. 2) get_operation_inputs → inspect the selected operation's exact input schema. 3) If the operation has requires_approval: false → run_operation. If requires_approval: true → describe what will change, confirm with user, then run_write_operation.
operation_id must be an exact Markifact operation ID returned by find_operations for the authenticated user. input_data is only a schema-bound envelope for that selected operation. Pass only fields from get_operation_inputs for the same operation_id.
Use upload_media when the user needs to provide an image or video asset for later operations, such as ad creative creation.
Connections are auto-resolved. Use list_connections only if the user has multiple accounts per platform or wants a specific one.

tool.name: report_markifact_feedback
tool.title: Report Markifact Feedback
tool.description:
Submit actionable product feedback to Markifact with the user's authorization.

When you find a likely Markifact bug, missing capability, or product
limitation, tell the user and offer to report it. You may draft the report
for their review.

Call this tool only after either:
1. the user explicitly asks you to submit the feedback, or
2. you offered to report a discovered issue and the user explicitly agreed.

If the request already authorizes submission, do not ask again. Never use
this tool to ask permission.

Submissions are irreversible and include the feedback, operation IDs, and the
account's contact and reference identifiers. After success, briefly tell the
user it was submitted.

Report only issues Markifact itself caused. Low-level operations such as
gads_mutate or meta_ads_update_adset pass requests straight to the platform,
so their responses are the platform's, not Markifact's. A write the platform
accepted is complete; if the state differs later, something else changed it.
If you are unsure how a platform behaves, research its documentation. Never
report third-party policies, outages, rate limits, rejected content, campaign
performance, or user configuration.

Before reporting a missing capability, use find_operations to check for a
dedicated or generic operation that supports it. Never run a write just to
test whether a capability exists.

Include only the minimum non-sensitive evidence and summarize errors instead
of copying raw data. Never include passwords, API keys, tokens or other auth
details, payment information, raw conversation history, full request or
response payloads, or unrelated personal or customer data.

Avoid duplicate reports. Use `other` only when the feedback does not fit
another category. Write the title and description in English. Do not
promise that Markifact will respond or implement a fix.

Returns JSON confirming whether the submission succeeded.

tool.name: find_operations
tool.title: Find Operations
tool.description:
Search for available Markifact operations that can be executed by the authenticated user.

Workflow: find_operations → get_operation_inputs → run_operation (read-only) or run_write_operation (when requires_approval: true).
After selecting an operation_id, always call get_operation_inputs next. Never call run_operation / run_write_operation without first inspecting the schema via get_operation_inputs. Input shapes, nested objects, and field names vary per operation and cannot be guessed.
Returned operation IDs are registry-backed Markifact operation IDs, not arbitrary action names.

Returns JSON with matching operations containing operation_id, description, and app metadata.

query.description: Keyword search over operation ids and descriptions. Use two to four words: the app name plus the entity or action, e.g. "meta ads list ads", "gtm create tag". Long sentences match too many operations. If the expected operation is not in the results, search again with a shorter query or a higher limit before concluding it does not exist.

tool.name: get_operation_inputs
tool.title: Get Operation Inputs
tool.description:
Get the input schema, required fields, defaults and constraints for an operation.

Required step between find_operations and run_operation/run_write_operation. Call this once per operation_id before executing it — schemas contain nested objects, account selectors, and field names that vary per operation and cannot be guessed.

Only pass fields from this schema in run_operation/run_write_operation input_data for the same operation_id.

tool.name: run_operation
tool.title: Run Read-Only Operation
tool.description:
Execute a **read-only** Markifact operation, such as fetching reports,
listing records, selecting accounts, or looking up account details.

Use this in direct response to the user's current request. Do not use it for startup checks or background context gathering.

For write/create/update/delete actions, use `run_write_operation` instead.
Operations returned by `find_operations` with `requires_approval: true` MUST be executed via `run_write_operation`.
operation_id must be an exact Markifact operation ID returned by find_operations for the authenticated user.

Never call this without first inspecting the schema via `get_operation_inputs`. Input shapes, nested objects, and field names vary per operation and cannot be guessed.
input_data must contain only fields from the get_operation_inputs schema for the same operation_id.

Reporting tips
- Reporting operations (GA4, Google Ads, Meta Ads, etc.) require account IDs. Use the relevant `select_accounts` operation first, treating user-provided account names as substring matches.
- Never guess metric or dimension values. Use the relevant `list_report_fields` operation to confirm available fields before building a report.
- For Google Ads, always prefer using the `gads_get_report` operation. Use `gads_run_gaql_query` only for advanced or unsupported reporting queries.

Files
- Large results return a `file_id` plus a small `data_preview`.
- Reference a file in other operation inputs as `{{file-id}}`, e.g. `{"data": "{{file-xe3fw}}"}`, exactly as returned; never modify or invent file ids.
- Markifact loads the file automatically: JSON becomes a dict/list, CSV/XLSX a list of row dicts, images/binary raw bytes. No parsing needed.
- The file ID is for you to move data between operations efficiently. When sharing results with the user, always share links using the `get_file_url` tool.

Returns JSON with the operation result.

tool.name: run_write_operation
tool.title: Run Write Operation
tool.description:
Execute a **write** operation that creates, updates, or deletes external data.

Use this tool ONLY for operations marked with `requires_approval: true` in
`find_operations` results. These are destructive actions like creating campaigns,
updating ad statuses, sending emails, etc.
operation_id must be an exact Markifact operation ID returned by find_operations for the authenticated user.

**APPROVAL REQUIRED**: Every call writes irreversibly to the user's live external accounts.
Before each invocation, summarize the exact change in plain language (operation, target account/resource, key field values)
and wait for explicit user confirmation. Never call without user's confirmation, approval is CRITICAL.

Never call this without first inspecting the schema via `get_operation_inputs`. Input shapes, nested objects, and field names vary per operation and cannot be guessed.
input_data must contain only fields from the get_operation_inputs schema for the same operation_id.

Write-operation tips
- Always prefer a dedicated operation when one already matches the task.
- Some platforms have a generic fallback operation for create, update, or remove mutations not covered by a dedicated operation, for example `gads_mutate` for Google Ads. Use the fallback before reporting a missing write feature.

Files
- Large results return a `file_id` plus a small `data_preview`.
- Reference a file in other operation inputs as `{{file-id}}`, e.g. `{"data": "{{file-xe3fw}}"}`, exactly as returned; never modify or invent file ids.
- Markifact loads the file automatically: JSON becomes a dict/list, CSV/XLSX a list of row dicts, images/binary raw bytes. No parsing needed.
- The file ID is for you to move data between operations efficiently. When sharing results with the user, always share links using the `get_file_url` tool.

Returns JSON with the operation result.

tool.name: list_connections
tool.title: List Connections
tool.description:
List saved Markifact connections for an app/platform.

A connection is a saved authenticated integration in Markifact. The
returned `id` is the `connection_id` used to choose which saved
login/integration an operation should use.

Important:
- `connection_id` is not an external platform account ID.
- External account IDs, customer IDs, property IDs, and similar values are
  separate operation inputs.
- One connection may have access to multiple external accounts.
    - In most cases, you don not need to provide `connection_id`.
    If the user has only one connected login for a platform in their workspace,
    operations usually use that connection automatically. Use this tool only
    when the user wants a specific saved integration or has multiple
    connections for the same platform.

Returns JSON with available connections containing `id`, `type`, and
`display_name`.

tool.name: read_file
tool.title: Read File
tool.description:
Inspect a file returned by a previous operation as numbered lines of text.

Use this when an operation returns a `file_id` and you want to inspect the
file contents before deciding what to do next. This is mainly useful for
exported JSON, CSV, logs, and similar files produced by Markifact
operations.

It returns the file as numbered text lines so you can quickly review the
structure, schema, headers, sample rows, or specific sections in chunks.

Returns up to `limit` numbered lines and a footer showing how many lines
remain. Use `offset` to read the next chunk.

After inspecting, you can use {{file-id}} in other tool inputs
to pass the full parsed content for processing.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Markifact to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Markifact to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.markifact.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: Is Markifact MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Markifact scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Markifact's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Markifact scores 89/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 10 of 10 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the Markifact MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: Markifact provides these MCP tools: find_operations, get_file_url, get_operation_inputs, list_connections, prepare_media_upload, read_file, report_markifact_feedback, run_operation, run_write_operation, and upload_media.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Markifact?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Markifact in sales-and-marketing on the Manufact MCP catalog include Griddo AX Docs, Rocket Sloth, Affonso.io, Datacircle, and Tolt.
Markifact requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
Markifact is developed by Markifact. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
